what's the difference between the swing desk and the day desk?

Kestrel splits its money into two desks, 50% each, and judges them separately so a losing one can't hide behind a winner. The swing desk holds stocks for days to weeks and decides once a day at 3:45pm New York time, 15 minutes before the close. It can hold up to 8 positions of at most 12.5% of its money, with a 7% stop-loss. The day desk is in and out the same day: it decides every 5 minutes, holds at most 3 positions of up to 33% each, makes no new trades in the last 30 minutes and sells everything 10 minutes before the close. A ticker can only be on one desk.

swing desk vs day desk, how are they different

Think of them as two separate traders sharing the account. The swing desk is the patient one: it looks at daily prices, makes one decision a day 15 minutes before the close (3:45pm ET on a normal day), and keeps positions for days or weeks. It spreads its half of the money over as many as 8 stocks, 12.5% each, and sells anything that falls 7% below its buy price. The day desk watches 5-minute prices, can hold 3 positions of up to 33%, and never keeps anything overnight. Each desk goes through study, paper and real money on its own.

Its list is a fixed watchlist plus up to 10 'stocks in play' picked each morning at 9:35.

what are the phases kestrel goes through?

Each desk moves on its own through four steps. Study: at least 30 calendar days and 20 trading days of watching, with no real orders; meanwhile it trades 'in its head' with pretend money. Plan review: it backtests every method, adds the study results and writes a plan, which may honestly say don't trade. Paper: you approve the plan and it trades fake money, in Alpaca's paper account or simulated on the Mac. Live: only if the paper results pass every rule and you confirm. A kill switch on a live desk sends it back to paper.

how does it pick which strategy to trade after studying?

It backtests every method on all the history it has and checks the study month. To be picked, a method needs a Sharpe of at least 0.5, a profit factor of 1.15 or more, a worst drop no bigger than 25% and at least 30 backtest trades. On top of that, swing needs 10+ graded buy opinions with a positive edge; day needs 10+ shadow trades that made money. Of the ones that pass, it picks the best Sharpe. If none pass, the plan says NO_TRADE and the desk keeps studying. You still have to approve the plan.

how does momentum work

Momentum is Stage 1's method on the swing desk. It ranks every stock on its list (the watchlist plus the 30 strongest stocks from the daily scan that it can afford) by its return over the last 12 months, skipping the most recent month. It buys from the top 20% as long as the stock is above its 200-day average. It sells when a stock drops out of the top half of the ranking or falls below its 200-day average. While the S&P 500 (SPY) is below its own 200-day average, it buys nothing new but keeps what it owns.
